title: Python async (asyncio), Part 2: inside asyncio's event loop
tldr: Part 1's gateway, now on real sockets: what a blocking socket does to one thread (about 1,460 ms), non-blocking sockets and BlockingIOError, and readiness notification with selectors (epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS, completion ports on Windows). Then one iteration of asyncio's loop read from CPython 3.14's source, call_soon and call_later, Futures (states, results, done callbacks), the Future at the bottom of every await chain, Tasks that drive coroutines step by step, and what asyncio.run does from start to finish. Gateway v2 adds a selector to Part 1's toy loop; gateway v3 runs on asyncio streams: 900 ms, then seller-b at 1,199 in 250 ms, and a failing seller stays inside its own Task. Then what breaks (busy loops, forgotten unregister, idle sockets, file descriptor limits, cross-thread calls, private internals), which I/O layer to pick, and an interview drill on what happens between await reader.readline() and your code resuming.
